findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the single writer that advances the inline `rich_sha` on a genuine wire change (e.g. co-located in `_advance_baselines` at persist) and confirm the compare path never writes it, so update-ownership and no-op-no-write are unambiguous.
evidence: Plan: 'store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] (8 bytes) inline in the binding … The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.'
Plan reuses `_advance_baselines` (reconcile.py:519) as 'the single existing writer unchanged' for the baseline, but does not say this writer also owns rich_sha.
T9 checklist: 'Who creates the state and when is defined' and 'Update concurrency / ownership is clear.'
findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` shared state names a CREATE site (inline beside `_BASELINE_FIELDS`) and a change-gated semantics, and asserts 'The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back' — but it does not name the WRITER that advances `rich_sha` when the rendered wire actually changes. The plan reuses `_advance_baselines` for the baseline but does not state whether that same single writer also updates `rich_sha`, leaving update-ownership/concurrency for the new field unspecified.
findings.location: Origin-gating section ('store a change-gated rich_sha … inline in the binding') and Scope: binding_store.py
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that `rich_sha` is advanced by the same `_advance_baselines` persist writer from `ctx.curr_snapshot`, gated on `sha256(rendered_wire)` differing from the stored value, and that no other path mutates it.

findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` state names its shape (8-byte sha256 of rendered wire), its change-gate discipline (no per-pass write), and that the compare is read-only, but it never names the WRITER: which function advances `rich_sha` and at what point in the pass. The plan is explicit that `_advance_baselines` is the single existing writer for the baseline and that the compare 'never writes back', which leaves the rich_sha write path unowned — is it a second writer, or is it folded into `_advance_baselines`?
findings.suggested_fix: State that `rich_sha` is advanced by the same single `_advance_baselines` writer at persist (change-gated on rendered-wire delta), so no second writer is introduced.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify `rich_sha` against the emission gates already in the plan: name the exact emit/push site that READS rich_sha and the decision it changes that the emit compare (outbound_field_diff.py:292) and origin-gating (`local != baseline`) do not already make — or drop rich_sha and rely on the existing compares.
evidence: Plan: 'store a change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) inline in the binding ... so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.'

Plan (step 1, emit compare): the send-fit and compare-fit are the identical transform so 'an already-synced body re-emits exactly once ... then converges' — i.e. emission is already gated by the compare.
Plan (origin-gating): 'a description update fires only when `local` differs from `baseline`' — a second, existing gate.

Code: outbound_field_diff.py:292 emits `changed['description']` only when `not _text_matches(fitted, canonical_remote.get('description',''))`; :277 wraps it in the `_suppressed_by_inbound` (local==baseline) guard. Neither reads a stored sha.

ABSENCE: no Scope entry or AC names an emit/push site that consults rich_sha; the git-delta AC only asserts rich_sha writes 0 entries on a no-op pass (a churn property), not that rich_sha changes any push decision.
findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` state is not shown to gate any push distinct from the two emission gates the plan already relies on (the emit compare `fitted != canonical_remote['description']` at outbound_field_diff.py:292, and origin-gating `local != baseline` at :277). The plan says rich_sha exists 'so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed' yet also states 'The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back' and names no code path that reads rich_sha to suppress a push the existing compares don't already suppress — a body equal to the remote is never emitted regardless of any sha.
findings.location: Origin-gating section ('store a change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` ... so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed'); Scope: `binding_store.py — inline change-gated rich_sha`; AC 'The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte rich_sha'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer cannot tell what rich_sha is FOR: if the emit compare and origin-gating already prevent an unchanged-wire push, rich_sha stores per-binding bytes that gate nothing, adding a new committed field (churn/space) with no consumer.

If rich_sha IS meant to gate something the compares miss (e.g. a benign Jira re-canonicalization the decode-on-compare doesn't absorb), that consumer and predicate are unspecified, so the field's contract is untestable beyond the no-op-pass churn assertion.

findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` per-binding state is a third emission gate whose necessity is not established by the plan's own logic: the plan already describes outbound description emit as fully gated by origin-gating (`local != baseline`) AND the once-only re-emit compare (`fitted != canonical_remote`), and states the compare 'stays comparison-only and never writes back' — but never names a read/consume site where `rich_sha` gates a push. The plan justifies rich_sha's SIZING (0.07 KB/version vs the rejected per-pass timestamp) but not what re-push it prevents that the existing baseline-diff + emit-compare do not.
findings.location: Plan §'Origin-gating so Jira-native constructs survive (AC5)'; §Scope (binding_store.py bullet); AC 'The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte rich_sha'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the DC-side render failure behavior: install a plain-text fallback for WikiTextCodec.to_wire / the CREATE path (mirroring the Cloud whole-codec fallback), or document why the DC renderer cannot raise.
evidence: Cloud bullet: 'install the whole-codec plain-text fallback'
DC bullet only states 'WikiTextCodec.to_wire delegates to wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki' with no fallback
backend.py:70 CREATE path 'render via the renderer/to_wire before the fit' — a render failure here would fail issue creation
findings.finding: The Cloud cutover installs a 'whole-codec plain-text fallback' for a render/encode failure, but the DC cutover (WikiTextCodec.to_wire delegating to render_markdown_to_wiki, and the CREATE path composing the renderer before fit) does not enumerate any equivalent fallback or error handling if the wiki renderer raises on unusual/malformed Markdown.
findings.location: The live cutover (both clients) — DC bullet; Scope: adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py and backend.py:70
scenarios: A Markdown body the wiki renderer cannot handle is synced/created on the DC path with the flag on, and the render call raises, failing the whole update/create with no graceful degradation to plain text.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a DC whole-codec plain-text fallback symmetric to Cloud: if render_markdown_to_wiki raises, to_wire (and the CREATE-path compose) fall back to the plain string, and surface the failure via a log/metric.

findings.finding: The cutover flag's DEFAULT state (on vs off in production) is never stated. The plan describes a rollback ('one revert') and a rollback test with 'the cutover flag off', but does not say whether the flag ships defaulting-on (a 100%-traffic behavior flip) or defaulting-off (opt-in). This is load-bearing for whether the cutover is a staged rollout or an all-traffic flip.
findings.location: Approach → 'Rollback' bullet; Scope → gated cutover; AC 'The cutover is flag-gated'
